title: Constellations
topic: How do scattered dots become one picture?

cards.title: A few dots on a white page
cards.text: About twenty small dots, some split into two colours, on a white page with nothing joining them. The plainest case to start from: they already half read as a loose ring.

cards.title: Dots in even rows on tan
cards.text: Small dots in mixed colours set in even rows on a tan ground. Equal spacing alone makes them one field before any line is drawn.

cards.title: Dots packed until they overlap
cards.text: Hundreds of painted dots of every size and colour, crowded until they cover each other. Past a certain crowd the dots stop being separate things and turn into a texture.

cards.title: Oil Sketch for "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte"
cards.text: A small oil sketch on panel built from separate dabs of colour. From a step back the dabs join into people on a riverbank: a crowd of dots turned into a picture, with no outlines.

cards.title: White and green dots drifting on blue
cards.text: White, green and pink dots on a blue ground, tiny on the left and large and crowded on the right. The change in size across the page gives the crowd a direction, as if it were moving.

cards.title: Dots thickening toward a centre
cards.text: Soft painted dots, thin at the edges of the sheet and crowded low in the middle. Closeness does the grouping: the eye finds one cluster where the dots sit tightest.

cards.title: Star Cluster in Hercules
cards.text: A print of the star cluster in Hercules, from a study made in June 1877. Real stars doing what the painted dots above do: crowding toward a middle until they read as one body.
cards.credit: Étienne Léopold Trouvelot, The Trouvelot Astronomical Drawings

cards.title: Disc of dots set in rings
cards.text: Small coloured dots set in ring after ring, from a tiny centre out to a clean round edge. Here the cluster is planned: a rule places every dot, and the outline is a circle.

cards.title: Ring of specks round a white middle
cards.text: Thousands of tiny coloured specks crowd into a ring and thin out to nothing, leaving a clean white circle inside. The empty middle is the shape; the dots only mark its edge.

cards.title: Watercolour ring dabbed with a cotton swab
cards.text: A loose ring of red, yellow and blue dabs, with stray ones drifting away at the edges. A label in the corner of the sheet gives the materials as watercolour and cotton swab.

cards.title: Burst of coloured dots round a hole
cards.text: Rows of bright dots run outward from an empty centre like rays, smaller toward the inside. Direction joins them: every row points back at the same missing middle.

cards.title: Total Eclipse of the Sun
cards.text: The sun's corona drawn round the black disc of the moon, as observed on 29 July 1878 at Creston, Wyoming Territory. Rays round a covered middle, as in the burst above, seen in the sky.
cards.credit: Étienne Léopold Trouvelot, The Trouvelot Astronomical Drawings

cards.title: The gap is part of the picture
cards.text: In the rings and bursts the eye reads the empty circle first and the dots second. A shape made of dots needs the space it leaves out as much as the dots themselves.

cards.title: Coloured dots strung on fine lines
cards.text: A close view of a drawing: rings of colour and small black knots sit along thin wavy lines. Once a line runs through them, the dots become stops on a path.

cards.title: Hand-drawn web of names in a circle
cards.text: A hand-drawn diagram: small labelled circles joined by curved arrows, all held inside one big circle. Pinterest's title names Mark Lombardi and speaks of diagrams of the uses and abuses of power.

cards.title: Collective dynamics of 'small-world' networks
cards.text: Shows that a few long links added to a tidy local web put every point only a few steps from any other: why a drawing of who knows whom curls into one ball.

cards.title: Network pulled into red and blue clumps
cards.text: A network of hair-thin links that pull the dots into dense red clumps and blue clumps, with a few long threads between. Where the links run, not where anyone put the dots, makes the picture.

cards.title: Graph drawing by force-directed placement
cards.text: A method for drawing a network: linked dots pull together like springs and all dots push apart, until the layout settles. Clumps like those above come out of it.

cards.title: Network so dense it reads as a ball
cards.text: Coloured dots on black with so many links between them that the whole thing becomes one fuzzy ball. With too many lines, the picture goes back to being a single dot.

cards.title: Euler's figure of the Königsberg bridges
cards.text: Figure 1 of Euler's paper on the seven bridges of Königsberg: a river, its bridges, and the pieces of land lettered A to D. The puzzle only needs to know what joins what.

cards.title: London Underground map, 1908
cards.text: A 1908 map of London's underground railways, each line in its own colour over a faint street plan. Stations are the dots, and the colour says which ones lie on one journey.

cards.title: Poster of rounded coloured routes
cards.text: Red, blue, green and yellow lines with rounded corners loop and cross on a pale poster, with a few single words set beside them. No dots at all, and it still reads as a map of stops.

cards.title: Tangle of thick coloured lines
cards.text: Thick painted lines in many colours wander over and under each other with no start and no end. Take the order out of a route map and the lines stop saying where anything is.

cards.title: Loops of coloured line
cards.text: Closed loops in blue, red, yellow and green, drawn loosely on top of one another. Each line ends where it began, so every loop turns into a large hollow dot.

cards.title: Mobile of yellow discs
cards.text: A hanging mobile: yellow discs from large to small on thin curved wires, against a grey-green wall. Dots lifted off the page, with the wire as the line between them.

cards.title: Blue discs on long thin wires
cards.text: A wider mobile of small blue discs, some turned edge-on, on wires thin enough to nearly vanish against the wall. The dots seem to float and the links are only guessed at.

cards.title: Orrery clock
cards.text: A gilded clock that carries small balls on arms inside metal rings: an orrery, a model of the planets going round. The same build as a mobile: each ball on its own arm, free to turn.

cards.title: Wide mobile of many small beads
cards.text: A long, low mobile carrying dozens of small coloured beads on a spread of fine wires. With this many dots the arms disappear and the whole thing reads as one drifting cloud.

cards.title: Room hung with coloured pieces
cards.text: A person stands in a room filled with small cup-like coloured pieces hung on threads from the ceiling. The dots now surround the viewer, and there is no one spot to see them all from.

cards.title: Rows of hung balls in a gallery
cards.text: A visitor looks up at a block of small balls hung in straight rows, shading from blue at the top to red at the bottom. The even grid of dots again, this time with depth.

cards.title: Small pictures joined by lines
cards.text: Dozens of small framed pictures joined by thin grey lines into a loose cloud. Swap each dot for a picture and the network starts to say what it is about.

cards.title: Tiny pictures scattered like dust
cards.text: Hundreds of small pictures, many of them old paintings, float at different sizes over a pale ground. There are no lines: only size and nearness hint at which ones belong together.

cards.title: Paintings and Calligraphy by Iga Ueno Literati
cards.text: An eight-panel folding screen from Japan carrying dozens of separate small paintings, fan shapes and sheets of calligraphy by fifty-six artists. Many pictures, laid out to be read as one.

cards.title: Tiny people circled with pencil loops
cards.text: Tiny figures seen from above, each with its shadow, scattered over cream paper, with coloured loops and hatching drawn round some of them. A drawn ring groups dots without touching them.

cards.title: Bright fibres branching on black
cards.text: A black-and-white image of bright fibres that meet at glowing knots and branch away again, like nerve cells under a microscope. Nobody placed these dots; the web looks grown.

cards.title: Tangle of light with bright knots
cards.text: White threads on black gather into a rough ball, with a bright point wherever several of them cross. Here the dots come second: threads meet, and a dot appears.

cards.title: Emergence of Scaling in Random Networks
cards.text: Shows that a network which keeps growing, each new point linking to points that already have many links, ends up with a few big hubs, like the bright knots above.

cards.title: Blue filaments round a bright core
cards.text: Fine blue-white strands fan out from a bright centre to a rim of small beads, on a dark ground. A web grown outward from one point, where the tangle above spreads from many.

cards.title: Stream network seen from the Space Shuttle
cards.text: A 1992 photograph from the Space Shuttle Endeavour over Zaire: woodland left standing along small streams traces a branching network across cleared land. A web that water grew.

cards.title: Chains of glowing shapes on black
cards.text: Hundreds of small glowing shapes, like galaxies in a telescope picture, line up along strands that meet and part across a black field. The dots themselves make the lines.

cards.title: Orion in Bayer's Uranometria
cards.text: The constellation Orion from Johann Bayer's star atlas, a copperplate engraving: stars as small bursts, with a man raising a club drawn over them. Before computers, one way to join dots was to draw a figure on top.

cards.title: Dunhuang star chart, north polar region
cards.text: A section of a hand-drawn star chart from Dunhuang, probably from about 700, showing the sky round the north pole. Stars are dots joined by short lines into named groups: the join made with a line, not a figure.

cards.title: The Celestial Map: Northern Hemisphere
cards.text: A woodcut of the whole northern sky on one disc, with animals and people drawn over the stars. Each figure holds its handful of stars together the way a label holds a group.

cards.title: Coloured pins stuck in a road map
cards.text: A road map crowded with round-headed pins in many colours and a few small numbered blocks. One pin for each thing, placed where it belongs on the map: the hand-made way to see where they bunch.

cards.title: John Snow's cholera map
cards.text: John Snow's 1854 street map of part of London, with a small black bar for each case of cholera. No lines join them: the bars pile up in one place and the cluster shows itself.

cards.title: Three old ways to join dots
cards.text: Draw a figure over them, as Bayer and Dürer did. Rule short lines between them, as on the Dunhuang chart. Or plot each one on a map and let the pile show, as Snow did.
